content:
Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the model forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at the data patterns:

## Example 1 (2024-08-05)
- History: Price started at ~67.96 and gradually increased to ~71.17
- Sentiment: Mostly positive, ending at 0.67
- Model forecasts: Start around 68.50-69.33, then gradually increase
- True outcomes: Start around 68.86 and continue increasing more strongly

Looking at the divergence:
- At day 1: Model 68.50 vs True 68.86 (underestimated by +0.36)
- At day 5: Model 68.11 vs True 72.65 (underestimated by +4.54)
- At day 10: Model 69.83 vs True 72.52 (underestimated by +2.69)

The model consistently underestimates prices, especially as prices climb higher.

## Example 2 (2024-08-02)
Similar pattern - model forecasts are generally below true outcomes.

Looking at the first few days:
- Day 1: Model 70.26 vs True 70.44 (off by +0.18)
- Day 5: Model 69.64 vs True 71.06 (off by +1.42)
- Day 10: Model 69.87 vs True 72.11 (off by +2.24)

## Example 3 (2024-07-30)
- Day 5: Model 69.48 vs True 70.44 (off by +0.96)
- Day 10: Model 69.91 vs True 72.65 (off by +2.74)

## Example 4 (2024-07-29)
- Day 4: Model 70.01 vs True 71.17 (off by +1.16)


- Day 9: Model 67.07 vs True 70.14 (off by +3.07)

## Example 5 (2024-07-23)
- Day 1: Model 65.95 vs True 65.79 (overestimated by -0.16)
- Day 6: Model 69.16 vs True 69.24 (off by +0.08)

I notice a consistent pattern of model underestimation, particularly as prices continue to climb. The deviations become more pronounced with each day
